International News · 16 Sources · 4 Regions

Daily Brief

The United States launched extensive retaliatory strikes against Iran overnight, hitting dozens of Revolutionary Guard targets including military command centers, missile facilities, and coastal defense sites [France 24, Al Jazeera, Globe and Mail, The Hindu]. Iranian state media reported three civilian deaths, including a two-year-old child, on Qeshm Island [France 24, Al Jazeera]. The escalation follows Iran's missile attack on US bases in Jordan, though Pakistan confirmed negotiations between Washington and Tehran remain ongoing [France 24]. In Europe, firefighters continue battling massive wildfires across southern regions, with French authorities allowing 84,000 evacuees to return home while over 220,000 were displaced since the blaze began [France 24, RFI]. The EU's crisis management chief called for increased prevention funding as climate change intensifies fire risks [RFI]. Meanwhile, Russia struck Ukraine with missiles reaching as far as Lviv near the Polish border, killing at least 13 people and forcing Poland to scramble fighter jets [Globe and Mail]. The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady despite persistent inflation [Le Monde, Financial Times], while a magnitude 7.1 earthquake in Japan's Kumamoto region has killed at least 23 people, disrupting supply chains for automakers including Nissan and Daihatsu [Globe and Mail, Nikkei Asia].

  • A magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck Kumamoto prefecture on Kyushu island Tuesday, killing at least 23 people with 63 injured
  • The most serious damage occurred at Aeon Mall shopping center in Kashima, where an explosion occurred after the quake while thousands were evacuating
  • Nissan and Daihatsu production remains halted due to the earthquake's impact on regional supply chains
